title: What is actually happening when Wi-Fi drops?

lines.text: What is actually happening in the air when your video call freezes and your Wi-Fi suddenly disconnects?
lines.caps: What happens in the *air | when your Wi-Fi *drops?

lines.text: Wi-Fi travels on invisible radio frequencies at two point four and five gigahertz.
lines.caps: Wi-Fi travels on invisible *radio | waves through the *air

lines.text: Your router and phone are constantly transmitting millions of packet bursts per second back and forth.
When physical barriers like concrete walls, metal ductwork, or a running microwave interfere, packets collide.
When too many data packets get corrupted, signal-to-noise ratio plummets below the receiver threshold.
The device and router lose handshaking synchronization, forcing the link to reset and re-negotiate.
lines.caps: Forces router and phone to *reset | and re-negotiate *channels!

lines.text: Placing your router high on a central shelf eliminates sixty percent of common household dead zones.
lines.caps: Keep your router *high | and central to kill dead *zones!
